Marta: Vendor (NordicCloud AS) just sent an invoice to Redwood Ltd and asked us to gross-up for a 15% Norwegian withholding tax. They didn't charge VAT. Should we pay the grossed amount or ask for docs? :thinking:

Victor: Don't pay grossed amount without proof. We need the vendor to show legal basis (Norwegian tax notice or certificate) and calculation. Who's the supplier's registered country/ORG no?

Marta: Invoice shows NO org: 921234567, amount EUR 8,500, service: "cloud engineering support". PDF attached in Coupa.

Liam: Quick tax note: Norway sometimes levies withholding on certain service categories to non-residents, but it's not automatic for generic consulting. Also, since invoiced to Redwood Ltd (UK), UK VAT/reverse charge rules are relevant. WHT is a separate issue and is generally the vendor's claim. We don't gross-up unless the contract states vendor will receive net after WHT or we have to withhold and remit.

Liam: Ask vendor to either (A) reissue invoice with 0% VAT and "reverse charge" wording if applicable, OR (B) provide Norwegian tax authority statement showing WHT applies to this payment and a signed calculation. If they want us to gross-up, they must supply a contract clause or tax ruling. We should also confirm the paying entity (Redwood Ltd).

Marta: I'll email them. Draft reply: "We cannot gross-up by default. Please provide documentation supporting Norwegian WHT and reissue invoice showing VAT treatment. Payment will be held until clarified." Thoughts?

Victor: LGTM. Tag TaxTeam and Legal if vendor pushes back. Also set payment to HOLD in AP system.
